# Harmonic for Hacker News Harmonic for Hacker News is an Android Hacker News client which is meant to be modern, fast and well thought out. You can find it on Google Play for download. This has been my personal side project since 2020 and since starting my PhD in 2021 the time I have to dedicate to Harmonic has decreased. My personal philosophy on side projects is that the most important thing is building something that is actually shipped. Since much of my knowledge on building Android apps is ~10 years old, Harmonic does not use Kotlin or the latest Android API's and is probably not the easiest app to dig into the source code of. However, it is shipped, and it works fairly well in my opinion at least. :) The purpose of open-sourcing Harmonic is thus mainly to enable interested users to submit pull requests fixing issues or adding features. I would like to still be able to find my way around the app's code so I am not looking for a full Kotlin rewrite but if you have something you'd like to see fixed or added I am very open to PR's. I'll still commit things myself when I have time. # Features * Basic account functionality: log in, vote, comment, and submit * Material 3 design with some nice animations * Several themes including full black * A ton of customization options, bordering on feature creep * Fast! steps.message:
## Diagnosis

**Root cause:** `StoriesFragment` has two completely separate story-loading paths, and the title/domain filters were only implemented in one of them.

| View | Type index | Load path | Filters applied? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Top / New / Best / Ask / Show / Jobs / Bookmarks | 0, 4–9 | placeholder → `loadStory()` per item | ✅ yes |
| **Last 24 hours / 48 hours / week** | **1, 2, 3** | `loadTopStoriesSince()` → `loadAlgolia()` | ❌ **no** |

The Algolia endpoint returns fully-populated stories in one batch, so they never pass through `loadStory()` — the only place `filterWords`/`filterDomains` were ever consulted. `loadAlgolia()`'s post-processing loop only handled `hideClicked`. Hence a story titled "…brain…" shows up in the 24h/48h views no matter what the user filters, exactly as reported, while filtering works fine on Top Stories.

A second, related defect: the "settings changed → reload" check was dead code. `hideJobs` was reassigned at the top of `onResume()`, so the later `if (hideJobs != SettingsUtils.shouldHideJobs(...))` was always `false`, and filter-pref changes had no comparison at all. So even with the filter honored, editing the filter list and returning from Settings left the offending story on screen until a manual pull-to-refresh.

## Fix

1. **Extracted `shouldFilterStory(Story)`** — one implementation of the title-word / url-domain match, null-safe on `title`/`url` (the Algolia list's index-0 header placeholder has both `null`) and skipping empty filter phrases (a stray comma in the pref used to produce an `""` phrase that matches every title and wipes the whole list).
2. **Applied it in `loadAlgolia()`** — the actual bug fix. The removal loop now also drops filtered stories, and iterates from `listIterator(1)` so the header placeholder is never touched. Added the missing `continue` after the `hideClicked` removal so a removed story isn't evaluated twice.
3. **Gated on a new `applyFilters` parameter** — `true` for the 24h/48h/week views, `false` for explicit searches, so searching for a term you've filtered still returns results.
4. **`loadStory()` now delegates** to the same helper, replacing the two duplicated loops (same behavior, one source of truth).
5. **Made pref changes take effect** — `onResume()` now compares the newly-read filter lists and `hideJobs` against the previous values *before* overwriting them and refreshes when they differ (skipped while searching). The values are also initialized in `onViewCreated()` ahead of the first `attemptRefresh()`, so the initial load is filtered too and this comparison doesn't fire spuriously at startup.

## Verification

- `./gradlew clean assembleDebug` → **BUILD SUCCESSFUL**, `app-debug.apk` produced.
- Ran a standalone simulation of the new helper plus the `loadAlgolia` removal loop: `"Your Brain Is Not a Computer"` and `"brain-computer interfaces"` are both removed for filter word `brain` (case-insensitive), a `bloomberg.com` story is removed by domain, unrelated stories survive, a story with a `null` url doesn't crash, and the header placeholder is preserved → PASS.

The only intentional behavior change beyond the fix is that search results are deliberately left unfiltered; all other views filter as before.
